description:
Add the approved repository-wide review policy to its canonical prose and registry-owned locations. Generated projections are updated only through their configured renderers so authoritative policy exists before review procedure begins consuming it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `.jit/invariants.toml` defines advisory invariant `pid-safety` with the approved statement that process-signaling code rejects sentinel or lossy PID conversions before operating-system invocation, including the `u32::MAX as i32 == -1` case that could produce `kill(-1, sig)`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The new invariant resolves at `@/inv/pid-safety` and appears in the renderer-owned invariant region of `AGENTS.md` without a hand-maintained duplicate.
- [hard] REQ-03: The hand-authored Coding Conventions section of `AGENTS.md` requires public APIs to document purpose and material contracts, including relevant errors or invariants, with examples for non-obvious usage or behavior.
- [hard] REQ-04: The hand-authored Testing Strategy section of `AGENTS.md` requires relevant success, boundary, failure, and concurrency coverage, with contextual examples including empty graphs, cycles, missing issues, and concurrent claims.
- [hard] REQ-05: Registry and Markdown projections affected by the policy changes are mechanically fresh, and unaffected projections are not rewritten without a changed configured input.
- [hard] REQ-06: The PID rule remains advisory unless the implementation identifies an existing deterministic rule or gate that mechanically enforces it.
title: Establish canonical review policy in repository sources
